q265.question: How does The Urantia Book say religious people should take part in social reform and politics?
q265.answer:
Paper 99 teaches that religion should not become organically involved "as a group" in the secular work of social reconstruction and economic readjustment, but that religious people may well become outstanding leaders of social reform "as individual citizens." Religion's part is not to run institutions directly but to supply moral stability and spiritual progress in a time of rapid change and to foster cosmic loyalty in the individual [99:1.2, 99:1.6, 99:3.15, 99:3.16].

This distinction comes from a sober diagnosis of institutionalized religion. Because institutionalized religion has itself become part of the social order that needs to be reconstructed, it is caught in a vicious circle in which it cannot reconstruct society without first reconstructing itself [99:2.1, 99:2.2].

1. As Individuals, Not as Groups

"⟦Q 99:2.3⟧Os religiosos devem funcionar, na sociedade, na indústria e na política, como indivíduos, não como grupos, nem como partidos ou instituições.⟦/Q⟧" [99:2.3]. For the moment a religious group acts as such outside of religious activities, it immediately becomes a political party, an economic organization, or a social institution [99:2.3]. Religious collectivism must therefore confine its efforts to the furtherance of religious causes [99:2.3, 99:3.15].

2. Two Ways Religionists Influence Society

The religionist is not unsympathetic with social suffering, civil injustice, or political tyranny [99:3.3]. Religion influences civilization directly by spiritualizing and idealizing the individual citizen, and indirectly as such individuals become influential members of various social, economic, and political groups [99:3.3]. A high civilization demands, first, the ideal type of citizen and, then, adequate social mechanisms by which such citizens may control its institutions [99:3.4]. Yet religionists are not automatically better reformers; they are of greater value only in so far as they have the social wisdom born of the sincere desire to love God supremely and to love every man as a brother [99:2.4].

3. Five Ways to Keep Religion Free from Secular Alliances

There is always the danger that religion will be distorted into the pursuit of false goals, as when in times of war nations prostitute their religion into military propaganda [99:3.8]. The following five safeguards are offered [99:3.9-3.14]:

A critically corrective philosophy [99:3.10]
Freedom from all social, economic, and political alliances [99:3.11]
Creative, comforting, and love-expanding fellowships [99:3.12]
Progressive enhancement of spiritual insight and the appreciation of cosmic values [99:3.13]
Prevention of fanaticism by the scientific mental attitude [99:3.14]

4. The Proper Social Role of the Church

The church must cease glorifying the political and economic orders of the past, and its only proper attitude consists in the teaching of nonviolence, peaceful evolution in place of violent revolution [99:2.5]. At the same time, though religion stands apart from secular activities, it must not hinder or retard the social co-ordination of human institutions [99:7.1]. Political science must reconstruct economics and industry by the techniques of the social sciences and the insights and motives supplied by religious living, and in that process religion provides a stabilizing goal beyond temporal objectives, a loyalty to a transcendent object [99:7.2]. Religion must act as "⟦Q 99:1.4⟧the cosmic salt which prevents the ferments of progression from destroying the cultural savor of civilization⟦/Q⟧" [99:1.4].

5. The Kingdom of Heaven Is Not a Social Institution

Early Christianity was entirely free from all civil and economic entanglements; only later institutionalized Christianity became a part of the political structure of Western civilization [99:3.1]. The kingdom of heaven is neither a social nor an economic order but a spiritual brotherhood of God-knowing individuals, and that brotherhood, as a result, produces amazing social repercussions [99:3.2].

Summary

The social engagement of religion that The Urantia Book describes is not "the politicizing of the church" but "the spiritualizing of the citizen." Religious groups stay with religious causes, and the individuals nurtured within them serve in society and politics as citizens of love and wisdom. The mission of religion is to create, sustain, and inspire such cosmic loyalty in the individual [99:2.3, 99:3.3, 99:3.16].

q266.question: Why does The Urantia Book say that religious growth is "always unconscious," and if so, what can we do?
q266.answer:
The Urantia Book says that growth, whether physical, intellectual, or spiritual, is always unconscious. A person cannot cause growth directly, but he can supply conditions favorable to it, and supplying those conditions is our part [100:3.7, 100:1.8].

Here "unconscious" does not mean that growth happens haphazardly by itself or that it takes place in the subconscious. It refers to creative activity occurring on the superconscious level of the mortal mind [100:1.9].

1. Growth Is Not Made but Grows

"⟦Q 100:3.7⟧Love thus grows; it cannot be created, manufactured, or purchased⟦/Q⟧" [100:3.7]. Just as social growth cannot be secured by legislation and moral growth is not had by improved administration, so spiritual growth is not produced mechanically [100:3.7]. Religion itself cannot be bestowed on, loaned to, or learned from others; it is a personal experience that grows in proportion to the growing quest for final values [100:1.7].

2. Unconscious Growth and the Superconscious

That religious growth is unconscious means that it is not an activity of the subconscious realms of human intellect but a creative activity on the superconscious level [100:1.9]. Paper 100 describes this superconscious as the zone of direct contact with the Thought Adjuster, the indwelling spirit reality [100:5.6]. So it says that "⟦Q 100:1.9⟧A experiência da compreensão da realidade inconsciente do crescimento religioso é a comprovação mais positiva da existência funcional da supraconsciência.⟦/Q⟧" [100:1.9].

3. What We Can Do: Supplying Conditions and Habits

Although growth itself is unconscious, the factors of growth can be deliberate [100:1.8]. The book names these habits that favor religious growth [100:1.8]:

Cultivated sensitivity to divine values
Recognition of religious living in others
Reflective meditation on cosmic meanings
Worshipful problem solving
Sharing one's spiritual life with one's fellows
Avoidance of selfishness and refusal to presume on divine mercy
Living as in the presence of God

It also says that the certain technique of fostering the potential of spiritual growth is to maintain an attitude of wholehearted devotion to supreme values [100:1.6]. Man's sole contribution to growth is the mobilization of all the powers of his personality, that is, living faith [100:3.7].

4. By Progress and Loyalty, Not by Results

True growth is judged not by results but by progress, and it shows itself in the elevation of ideals, the deepening of value recognition, and the strengthening of loyalty to supreme values [100:1.3]. So the book counsels, "⟦Q 100:1.4⟧Vivei lealmente hoje — crescei —, e o amanhã responderá por si.⟦/Q⟧." [100:1.4], and adds the comparison that the quickest way for a tadpole to become a frog is to live loyally each moment as a tadpole [100:1.4]. Conversely, the person who is too busy to grow is in danger of spiritual fixation, and the chief obstacles to growth are prejudice and ignorance [100:1.2].

5. Conflict Is the Channel of Growth

New religious insights arise out of conflicts that call for choosing better habits of reaction, and there can be no growth without psychic conflict and spiritual agitation [100:4.1, 100:4.2]. Unconscious growth is not passivity; it accumulates quietly through such choices. The book adds that the great problem of religious living is to unify the soul powers of the personality by the dominance of love, and that spiritual growth yields lasting joy and the peace that passes all understanding [100:4.3].

Summary

Spiritual growth is a creative process that takes place in the superconscious, which we cannot manufacture directly. But we can supply its conditions through wholehearted devotion to supreme values, worship and meditation, sharing, and the overcoming of selfishness. Since "⟦Q 100:1.7⟧nobility itself is always an unconscious growth⟦/Q⟧", the way of growth is not to measure results but to live each day loyally [100:1.7, 100:1.8, 100:3.7].

q267.question: How does The Urantia Book evaluate sudden conversion experiences and mystical experiences?
q267.answer:
The Urantia Book acknowledges that sudden conversions can really happen, but it says that they are neither the only way nor a necessary process of spiritual growth. It also clearly warns that mystical experience may sometimes be a means of genuine spiritual communion but is dangerous when habitually sought, and that trance or vision states should not be pursued as religious experience [100:5.3, 100:5.8].

1. Gradual Growth and Crisis Conversion

The awareness of God-consciousness may grow naturally and gradually, or it may be experienced at certain junctures, as in a crisis [100:5.3]. The Apostle Paul experienced a sudden and spectacular conversion on the Damascus road, and Gautama Siddhartha had a similar experience the night he sat alone seeking to penetrate the mystery of truth [100:5.3]. But "⟦Q 100:5.3⟧many true believers have progressed in the spirit without sudden conversion⟦/Q⟧" [100:5.3]. Whichever way one arrives, there follows a new reorientation of personality and a new standard of values [100:2.8]. The progress of religious growth leads from stagnation through conflict to co-ordination, from the bondage of fear to the liberty of divine sonship [100:5.2].

2. What Happens in a True Conversion

Most of the phenomena associated with conversion are entirely psychologic, but now and then there are experiences which are also spiritual in origin [100:5.4]. When the mental mobilization is total and the motivation of loyalty to the divine idea is perfect, there very often occurs a sudden down-grasp of the indwelling spirit to synchronize with the superconscious mind of the believing mortal. This unified intellectual and spiritual experience is a conversion that goes beyond psychological processes [100:5.4]. On the other hand, "⟦Q 100:5.5⟧Por si, todavia, uma emoção só indica uma conversão falsa; deve ter-se fé, tanto quanto sentimentos.⟦/Q⟧." [100:5.5]

3. The Dangers of Mysticism

Mysticism may sometimes be a means of genuine spiritual communion, but it can degenerate into a technique of withdrawal from reality, and prolonged isolation of personality is not desirable [100:5.8]. The mystical state is characterized by diffusion of consciousness with vivid islands of focal attention, and such states draw consciousness toward the subconscious rather than the superconscious [100:5.9]. The book lists factors that favor mystic experience, such as physical fatigue, fasting, psychic dissociation, profound sexual impulses, fear, anxiety, rage, and wild dancing, and says that much of what arises under such conditions has its origin in the subconscious [100:5.10]. Altogether too much of the uprush of memories from the unconscious levels of the human mind has been mistaken for divine revelations and spirit leadings [100:5.7]. When divine beings revealed themselves to certain persons in the past, it was not because of their trances but in spite of all such phenomena [100:5.6].

4. The Example of Jesus

However favorable the conditions may have been, Jesus of Nazareth never resorted to such methods for communion with the Father, and he had no subconscious delusions or superconscious illusions [100:5.11]. The direct communion with his Thought Adjuster that Jesus enjoyed in the later years of his life should not be confused with so-called mystical experiences [100:5.10].

5. The Better Way

Rather than seeking conversion, the better approach to the morontia zones of possible contact with the Thought Adjuster is through "⟦Q 100:5.7⟧living faith and sincere worship, wholehearted and unselfish prayer⟦/Q⟧" [100:5.7]. The more healthful attitude of spiritual meditation is found in reflective worship and the prayer of thanksgiving [100:5.10].

Summary

The Urantia Book does not deny dramatic conversions, but it does not make them the standard. True conversion occurs not through emotion but when faith and wholehearted loyalty are present together, while mystical states carry a great danger of being drawn down into the subconscious. The healthy path of spiritual progress is living faith, sincere worship, unselfish prayer, and the prayer of thanksgiving [100:5.5, 100:5.7, 100:5.10].

q268.question: What does it mean that the uniqueness of Jesus' personality lay "in its symmetry rather than its perfection"?
q268.answer:
Section 7 of Paper 100 says that the unique feature of Jesus' personality was "⟦Q 100:7.1⟧not so much its perfection as its symmetry, its exquisite and balanced unification⟦/Q⟧" [100:7.1]. This means that Jesus was not someone who excelled to an extreme in one single virtue, but that qualities seemingly opposed to one another were harmonized in one personality, so that he was never one-sided. And this is a hope for us. For although the average person cannot attain the high perfection of character that Jesus achieved, the book says it is altogether possible to develop a strong and unified personality along the lines of his personality [100:7.1].

1. Virtues in Pairs

The book shows Jesus' balance through contrasts. He was surcharged with divine enthusiasm but never became fanatical; he was emotionally active but never flighty; he was imaginative but always practical. He was courageous but never reckless, prudent but never cowardly, sympathetic but not sentimental, pious but not sanctimonious [100:7.4]. The reason: "⟦Q 100:7.4⟧E era assim tão bem equilibrado, porque era perfeitamente unificado.⟦/Q⟧." [100:7.4]

2. Sincerity and Common Sense

Jesus was free from hypocrisy, lived as he taught, and was loyal to all truth [100:7.2]. At the same time his ministry was practical, his plans were characterized by sanctified common sense, and he was free from all freakish, erratic, or hysterical tendencies [100:7.3]. He was candid but always kind, and while he made no secret of his love for the sinner and his hatred of sin, he was perfectly fair [100:7.11].

3. Gladness and Controlled Enthusiasm

He was not a man of sorrows but a soul of gladness, and his constant word of exhortation was "⟦Q 100:7.9⟧Be of good cheer⟦/Q⟧," yet he was not a blind optimist [100:7.9, 100:7.13]. He was filled with enthusiasm for the gospel of the kingdom, but he controlled his enthusiasm; it never controlled him [100:7.12]. His unspiritual brethren thought he was beside himself, but the onlooking universe appraised him as the example of sanity [100:7.12].

4. Courage and Patience, Indignation and Mercy

His courage was equaled only by his patience. When pressed to act prematurely, he would only reply, "⟦Q 100:7.14⟧My hour has not yet come⟦/Q⟧"; he was often indignant at evil, but his indignation against sin never led to anger at the sinner [100:7.14]. His courage was born of faith and controlled by discrimination and reason [100:7.15]. He was original, yet he did not overlook the gems of truth in the teachings of his predecessors, and the most original of his teachings was the emphasis of love and mercy in the place of fear and sacrifice [100:7.5].

5. The Root of That Balance: Trust in God

All this balance came from a childlike trust in God. His faith was perfect but never presumptuous, and it was not shaken by disappointment, persecution, or apparent failure [100:7.7]. He reverenced true holiness and respected even the faulty worship of his fellows, yet this did not deter him from assaulting the errors of human belief [100:7.16]. He was gentle and unassuming in his personal life, and yet he was the perfected man of a universe [100:7.17]. Jesus was the perfectly unified human personality, and today he still unifies human experience, unifies life, and ennobles character [100:7.18]. So the book says that the most effective presentation of Jesus is to point to him and say, "Behold the man!", that is, to show his life itself [100:7.1].

Summary

"Symmetry" means the state in which Jesus' virtues checked and complemented one another to form one harmonious whole. Because enthusiasm and restraint, courage and prudence, candor and kindness were present together, he fell neither into fanaticism nor into sentimentality. Though we fall short of his perfection, we can follow the lines of his balance and unification, and that is the climax of religious living [100:7.1, 100:7.4, 100:7.18].

q269.question: What does it mean that the science and cosmology of The Urantia Book are "not inspired," and what does this imply for the book's authority?
q269.answer:
In section 4 of Paper 101, "The Limitations of Revelation," the revelators themselves declare, "⟦Q 101:4.2⟧A cosmologia nessas revelações não é inspirada.⟦/Q⟧." [101:4.2] This means that the book's statements on physical science and cosmology are not unchangeable truths guaranteed by divine inspiration but are presented within the limits of co-ordinating and sorting the knowledge that humans already had at the time of writing [101:4.2]. By contrast, the historic facts and religious truths are distinguished as things that will stand on the records of the ages to come [101:4.2].

1. The Law of Revelation: No Premature Knowledge

"⟦Q 101:4.1⟧The laws of revelation hamper us greatly by their proscription of the impartation of unearned or premature knowledge⟦/Q⟧." [101:4.1] The revelators say that they are very rigorously limited by the instructions of their superiors, so that they are not at liberty to anticipate the scientific discoveries of a thousand years, and that even when they foresee new developments, they are forbidden to include humanly undiscovered facts in the revelation [101:4.2].

2. They Know in Advance That Revisions Will Come

The revelators say that they know full well that within a few short years many of their statements regarding the physical sciences will stand in need of revision as a result of new discoveries [101:4.2]. Any cosmology presented as part of revealed religion is destined to be outgrown in a very short time [101:4.1], and they see no way of overcoming this difficulty, either now or in the future [101:4.2].

3. A Warning: Do Not Discard Religious Truth because of Cosmology

The reason for stating this limitation is clear: when future students discover apparent errors in the cosmology associated with a revelation, they are tempted to discard even the genuine religious truth it contains [101:4.1]. The reader must therefore read with a distinction between the time-bound limitation of scientific statements and spiritual truth. In the last analysis religion is to be judged by its fruits, according to the manner and extent to which it exhibits its own inherent and divine excellence [101:4.4]. Indeed, religion is said to survive even its contamination with erroneous cosmologies and false philosophies [101:3.1].

4. Five Values of Presenting a Cosmology Nonetheless

Statements about cosmology are not inspired, yet they are of great value in that they at least transiently clarify knowledge by the following [101:4.5-4.10]:

The reduction of confusion by the authoritative elimination of error [101:4.6]
The co-ordination of known or about-to-be-known facts and observations [101:4.7]
The restoration of lost knowledge concerning events in the distant past [101:4.8]
The supplying of information to fill in vital missing gaps in otherwise earned knowledge [101:4.9]
Presenting cosmic data in such a manner as to illuminate the spiritual teachings of the accompanying revelation [101:4.10]

5. Distinguishing Truth from Inspiration

"⟦Q 101:4.3⟧Truth is always a revelation⟦/Q⟧" [101:4.3]: when it comes through the indwelling Adjuster it is autorevelation, and when it comes through some celestial agency or personality it is epochal revelation [101:4.3]. Yet even though revelation is invariably a spiritual phenomenon, truth may be but relatively inspired [101:4.5]. The book sums this up in the words "⟦Q 101:4.2⟧Conquanto o discernimento divino ou espiritual seja uma dádiva, a sabedoria humana deve evoluir.⟦/Q⟧." [101:4.2] Revelation is a technique for saving ages upon ages of time in sifting out the errors of evolution [101:5.1], but the distinction remains that science deals with facts and religion with values, two different domains [101:5.2].

Summary

The words "not inspired" are an honest boundary line that The Urantia Book draws for itself. Its physical science and cosmology are a co-ordination of the knowledge of the time and so may be revised, while its religious truths and spiritual teachings are to be judged separately, by their fruits. The key counsel of this passage is therefore not to discard the spiritual truth of the revelation because its scientific details become outdated [101:4.1, 101:4.2, 101:4.4].

q270.question: How do "belief" and "faith" differ in The Urantia Book?
q270.answer:
The Urantia Book distinguishes the two: accepting a teaching as true is only "belief," and it reaches the level of "faith" only when that belief actually motivates life and dominates the mode of living [101:8.1]. Belief is the content to which the mind has agreed, while faith is the living experience in which that content moves one's life.

1. Definition: Whether It Dominates Life

"⟦Q 101:8.1⟧A aceitação de um ensinamento como verdadeiro não é fé; é mais uma crença.⟦/Q⟧." [101:8.1] Neither is certainty nor conviction in itself faith; a state of mind becomes faith only when it actually dominates the mode of living [101:8.1]. Faith is a living attribute of genuine personal religious experience, the attitude that believes truth, admires beauty, and reverences goodness, yet worships not them but God alone, who is all of these personified [101:8.1].

2. Belief Fixates, Faith Liberates

"⟦Q 101:8.2⟧A crença fixa, a fé liberta.⟦/Q⟧." [101:8.2] Belief is always limiting and binding, while faith is expanding and releasing. Living faith is more than an association of noble beliefs or an exalted system of philosophy; it is a living experience concerned with spiritual meanings, divine ideals, and supreme values, a life that is God-knowing and man-serving [101:8.2].

3. What Belongs to the Group and What Belongs to the Individual

Beliefs may become group possessions, but faith must be personal. Theologic beliefs can be suggested to a group, but faith can rise up only in the heart of the individual religionist [101:8.2]. Paper 99 says the same thing, urging that the word "faith" be allowed to stand for the individual's relation to God rather than for the creedal formulation of what some group has agreed upon [99:5.7]. What unites religionists should be a goal, not a creed [99:5.7].

4. When Faith Becomes a Traitor

Faith betrays its trust when it denies reality and tries to confer on its devotees a supposed knowledge, and when it compromises intellectual integrity [101:8.3]. Living faith does not evade its obligation to solve problems, and it does not foster bigotry, persecution, or intolerance [101:8.3]. Nor does it shackle the creative imagination or maintain an unreasoning prejudice toward scientific discovery; rather it constrains the religionist heroically to live the golden rule [101:8.4]. So the book says, "⟦Q 101:8.4⟧O zelo da fé está de acordo com o conhecimento, e os seus esforços são o prelúdio de uma paz sublime.⟦/Q⟧." [101:8.4]

5. How Faith Shows Itself

True spiritual faith shows itself more in life's reactions than in words. The book lists twelve such marks, among them trusting the goodness of God even in bitter disappointment, having profound courage and confidence even amid calamity, maintaining poise even amid the most severe suffering, and worshiping God under all circumstances [101:3.4-3.16]. Faith unites moral insight with conscientious discrimination of values [101:1.6], and religion lives and moves not by seeing and feeling but by faith and insight [101:1.4]. This faith-insight, or spiritual intuition, is said to be the endowment of the cosmic mind in association with the Thought Adjuster [101:3.2]. Therefore the deeply enlightened person at last realizes that to doubt God or distrust his goodness is to prove untrue to the indwelling Adjuster [101:1.7].

Summary

Belief is a state of mind that agrees something is true; faith is the living experience in which that truth dominates and moves one's life. Belief fixates and can be shared by a group, but faith liberates and grows only in the heart of the individual. And true faith keeps intellectual integrity and bears fruit in tolerance, service, and the practice of the golden rule [101:8.1, 101:8.2, 101:8.4].

q271.question: What does each of science (knowledge), philosophy (wisdom), religion (experience), and revelation do, and how do they differ from one another?
q271.answer:
Section 3 of Paper 102 sets knowledge and wisdom, religion and revelation side by side and contrasts their roles. Put simply, science leads to fact consciousness, religion to value consciousness, philosophy to co-ordinating consciousness, and revelation to the consciousness of true reality [102:3.5]. These four are not competitors but different channels that help the human personality become aware of the whole of reality.

1. What Each Pursues

"⟦Q 102:3.12⟧A investigação do conhecimento constitui a ciência; a busca da sabedoria é filosofia; o amor por Deus é religião; a sede da verdade é uma revelação.⟦/Q⟧." [102:3.12] Science deals with facts, religion is concerned with values, and philosophy endeavors to unify the meanings of both [101:5.2]. Science seeks to analyze and classify the segmented parts of the cosmos, religion grasps the idea of the whole, philosophy attempts to bring the two into agreement, and where philosophy fails, revelation succeeds [102:3.10].

2. Their Effects on People and Society

The book contrasts how the four realms deal with people [102:3.6-3.8]:

Science (knowledge): places and sorts men and originates social strata [102:3.6, 102:3.7]
Religion: leads to serving men and loving them, even as yourself [102:3.6, 102:3.7]
Wisdom (philosophy): does justice to differing men and leads to a better fellowship [102:3.6, 102:3.7]
Revelation: liberates and glorifies man and discloses his capacity for partnership with God [102:3.6, 102:3.7]

In terms of brotherhood as well, science vainly strives to create the brotherhood of culture, religion brings into being the brotherhood of the spirit, philosophy strives for the brotherhood of wisdom, and revelation portrays the eternal brotherhood, the Paradise Corps of the Finality [102:3.8].

3. What They Give Concerning Personality and God

Knowledge yields pride in the fact of personality, wisdom is the consciousness of its meaning, religion is the cognizance of its value, and revelation is the assurance of personality survival [102:3.9]. Concerning God, science indicates Deity as a fact, philosophy presents the idea of an Absolute, religion envisions God as a loving spiritual personality, and revelation affirms the unity of these three and presents him as our Father [102:3.11]. Science is satisfied with first causes, religion with supreme personality, and philosophy with unity, but revelation affirms that these three are one and that all are good [102:3.15].

4. The Order of Idea and Experience

"⟦Q 102:3.13⟧Na ciência, a idéia precede à expressão da sua realização; na religião, a experiência da realização precede à expressão da idéia.⟦/Q⟧." [102:3.13] The book also contrasts the tendency of evolution to make God manlike with the tendency of revelation to make man Godlike [102:3.14]. Religious experience is the realization of the consciousness of having found God, and the one who has found God does not seek to boast of it but seeks loving service-contact with his less enlightened fellows, so that true religion leads to increased social service [102:3.4].

5. What Binds Them All Together

When the consciousness of fact, of value, and of true reality is co-ordinated and joined with belief in the survival possibilities of personality, there results the realization of personality reality [102:3.5]. And it is the indwelling Thought Adjuster that attaches the feeling of reality to man's spiritual insight [102:3.12]. Revealed religion, as the unifying element of human existence, unifies history and co-ordinates the various sciences [102:4.6].

Summary

Science knows facts, philosophy co-ordinates their meanings, religion experiences values, and revelation shows that all of them are one reality. Where science sorts people, religion makes us love them, wisdom does them justice, and revelation raises them to partnership with God. When these four are co-ordinated in balance, man becomes aware of the maximum of existence [102:3.5, 102:3.7, 102:3.11].

q272.question: Please explain, in connection with "morontia mota," why science and religion are not easily harmonized.
q272.answer:
The Urantia Book explains that the fundamental reason science and religion are hard to harmonize is man's ignorance of the intervening domain, the "morontia world" [103:6.7]. Local universe reality consists of three degrees, matter, morontia, and spirit, but mortals do not yet possess "mota," the ability to perceive the bridging morontia level [103:6.7, 103:6.8].

1. The Universe Seen from Without and from Within

When man analyzes the universe by the senses and mental perception, the cosmos appears to be mechanical and energy-material [103:6.4]. Conversely, viewed only from within personality experience, all creation appears to be spiritual [103:6.3]. "⟦Q 103:7.6⟧Do exterior, olhando para o interior, o universo pode parecer material; do interior, olhando para o exterior, o mesmo universo parece ser totalmente espiritual.⟦/Q⟧." [103:7.6] That is why no logical and consistent philosophy of the universe can be built on the postulates of either materialism or spiritism alone [103:6.5].

2. What Is Mota?

"⟦Q 103:6.7⟧A razão é a técnica de entendimento das ciências; a fé, a técnica do discernimento interior aplicado à religião; a mota é a técnica do nível moroncial.⟦/Q⟧." [103:6.7] Mota is a supermaterial reality sensitivity having for its substance knowledge-reason and for its essence faith-insight; it is a superphilosophical reconciliation of reality perception which is nonattainable by material personalities [103:6.7]. The morontia angle of approach is said to erase all divergence between the findings of the physical sciences and the functioning of the spirit of religion [103:6.7]. The fact that religion is always characterized by paradox likewise results from this lack of morontia mota [102:3.2].

3. The Failure of Metaphysics

Many mortals constructed metaphysics in an attempt to span the chasm between science and religion, but it has proved more confusing than illuminating, a well-meant but futile effort to compensate for the absence of mota [103:6.7]. When philosophy leans on metaphysics, it inevitably becomes skeptical and confused [103:6.14].

4. The Gap That Revelation Fills

"⟦Q 103:6.8⟧A metafísica tem-se revelado como sendo um fracasso; a mota, o homem não a pode perceber.⟦/Q⟧." [103:6.8] Revelation is therefore the only technique that can compensate for the absence of the truth sensitivity of mota in a material world [103:6.8], and it is evolutionary man's only hope of bridging the morontia gulf [103:6.13]. Revelation does not originate science or religion; it co-ordinates both with the truth of reality [103:7.8]. The highest philosophy attainable by mortals must be founded jointly on the reason of science, the faith of religion, and the truth insight afforded by revelation [103:6.15].

5. The Attitude Required of Us

What both science and religion need is more searching and fearless self-criticism [103:7.7]. Their harmony cannot succeed without a sincere desire to follow truth wherever it may lead [103:7.5]. Moreover, nothing can be absolutely proved in the mortal state; both science and religion are founded on assumptions, and only on the morontia level are they partially proved by mota logic [103:7.10]. The ascending human goes inward for the experience of God and at the same time outward for the understanding of the material cosmos, and the union of science and religion is part of the long Paradise ascension experience [103:7.3, 103:7.4]. Until then, science discovers the material world, religion evaluates it, and philosophy endeavors to interpret its meanings by co-ordinating the two [103:7.15].

Summary

Science views the universe from without and religion from within, so the same universe appears different. Mortals do not yet have mota, the morontia sense that unites the two, and metaphysics has not been able to take its place. Revelation fills that gap, and we should respect science and religion together, with self-criticism and a desire for truth [103:6.7, 103:6.8, 103:7.5].

q273.question: How has the concept of the Trinity been revealed and changed in Urantia history, and how is the Christian Trinity evaluated?
q273.answer:
Paper 104 relates that the truth of the Paradise Trinity was revealed to Urantia several times but was each time obscured or transformed. As for the Christian concept of the Trinity, it judges that "⟦Q 104:1.13⟧though the Christian concept of the Trinity erred in fact, it was practically true with respect to spiritual relationships⟦/Q⟧" [104:1.13].

1. Three Revelations

The first revelation was made by the staff of Prince Caligastia about five hundred thousand years ago, but it was lost in the unsettled times that followed the planetary rebellion [104:1.1]. The second presentation was made by Adam and Eve in the first and second gardens; the Trinity concept of the Sethites persisted in Mesopotamia and Egypt and especially in India, where it was perpetuated in Agni, the Vedic three-headed fire god [104:1.2]. The third presentation was made by Machiventa Melchizedek, and its symbol was the three concentric circles he wore on his breastplate [104:1.3]. But most of his followers thought of the Trinity as the three Most Highs of Norlatiadek, and very few grasped even dimly the Paradise union of Father, Son, and Spirit [104:1.3].

2. Traces in the Religions of the East

Through the Salem missionaries the teachings of Melchizedek spread through Eurasia and North Africa, and later they were so mixed with evolutionary triad concepts that the two became hard to distinguish [104:1.4]. Among the Hindus the concept appeared as Being, Intelligence, and Joy, and later as Brahma, Siva, and Vishnu [104:1.5]. In Buddhism there developed the doctrines of Teacher, Law, and Brotherhood, and, in the northern branch, of Supreme Lord, Holy Spirit, and Incarnate Savior [104:1.6]. The book stresses that these were true trinitarian postulates, a threefold manifestation of the one God, and that a true Trinity is not an aggregation of three separate gods [104:1.7].

3. The Tension with Monotheism

The Hebrews knew of the Trinity from the traditions of the Kenites, but their monotheistic zeal for Yahweh so eclipsed this teaching that by the time of Jesus the Elohim doctrine had been practically eradicated [104:1.8]. Muslims too found it difficult to distinguish between a polytheism that worships three gods and a triune manifestation of one God [104:1.9]. The Trinity concept takes root best in a religion that combines a firm monotheism with doctrinal elasticity [104:1.9].

4. Jesus and Early Christianity

Jesus taught his apostles the truth regarding the persons of the Paradise Trinity, but they thought he spoke figuratively [104:1.10]. The first Trinity of Christianity was proclaimed at Antioch and consisted of God, his Word, and his Wisdom [104:1.11]. Paul knew of the Paradise Trinity but seldom preached about it, and he confused Jesus, the Creator Son of the local universe, with the Eternal Son of Paradise [104:1.11]. The Christian Trinity that began to gain recognition near the close of the first century actually consisted of the Universal Father, the Creator Son of Nebadon, and the Mother Spirit of the local universe [104:1.12].

5. True in Spirit, Erroneous in Fact

The difficulty of the Christian concept lay in holding that the Second Person of Deity once dwelt on Urantia. The book says, "⟦Q 104:1.13⟧while in spirit this is true, in actuality it is not a fact⟦/Q⟧" [104:1.13]. For the Michael Creators fully embody the divinity of the Eternal Son, but they are not the absolute personality [104:1.13]. Since the time of Jesus the factual identity of the Paradise Trinity had not been known on Urantia until these revelatory disclosures [104:1.13].

6. Why the Trinity Concept Is Needed

The book explains that trinitarianism grew out of the experiential protest against the impossibility of conceiving a solitary Deity unrelated to other personalities. "⟦Q 104:2.2⟧A personalidade na Deidade exige que tal Deidade exista em relação a outra Deidade igual e pessoal.⟦/Q⟧." [104:2.2] The Trinity concept also helps us understand the interrelationship of love and law [104:2.3]. The Trinity is not a personality, but it is a true reality emerging from the union of the three Deities; justice, for example, is not a personal act but a collective function of the Trinity [104:2.4, 104:2.5].

Summary

The truth of the Trinity was revealed again and again, through the staff of Caligastia, through Adam and Eve, and through Machiventa Melchizedek, but each time it was obscured and left only traces in various religions. The Christian Trinity contained a factual error in confusing the Creator Son with the Eternal Son, yet it was true in spiritual relationships, and this revelation makes its factual identity known once more [104:1.1-1.3, 104:1.13].

q274.question: What kind of concept is the "I AM," and how is it related to the Universal Father whom we worship?
q274.answer:
The "I AM" is a philosophic postulate that the finite mind sets up in order to think about the absolute origin of all reality. The philosophers of the universes attribute the absolute primal causation in infinity to the Universal Father functioning as the infinite, eternal, and absolute I AM [105:1.1]. In other words, the I AM is not some God other than the Universal Father; it is a concept pointing to the whole of infinity, which goes beyond the Father as we know him. The book makes clear that in all personal meanings and values this concept is synonymous with the First Person of Deity, the Universal Father of all personality [105:1.2].

1. Why Such a Concept Is Needed

This idea is so remote from human experiential comprehension that it risks distorting meanings and misunderstanding values [105:1.2]. Nevertheless, it gives finite beings some basis for an attempted approach to understanding absolute origins and infinite destinies [105:1.2]. Because the finite mind must have a starting point, it postulates a "first" moment for the sake of thought, even though reality never had a true beginning [105:1.5, 105:2.2].

2. The Nature of the I AM

"⟦Q 105:1.3⟧O EU SOU é o Infinito; o EU SOU é também a infinitude.⟦/Q⟧." [105:1.3] As an existential concept, the I AM is neither deified nor undeified, neither actual nor potential, neither personal nor impersonal [105:1.4]. No qualification can be applied to the Infinite except the statement that the I AM is [105:1.4].

3. The Father We Experience and the I AM We Postulate

Our comprehension of the Universal Father is a personal experience, and God is comprehensible to us as our spiritual Father [105:1.6]. But the experiential, worshipful concept of the Father must always be less than the philosophic postulate of the infinity of the I AM [105:1.6]. The book distinguishes the Father, the phase of the Infinite that we perceive in actual experience within personality, from the I AM, the hypothesis concerning all that we feel to be unknowable about the First Source and Center [105:1.6]. And it says that the face which this Infinite turns toward all universe personalities is "⟦Q 105:1.8⟧the face of a Father, the Universal Father of love⟦/Q⟧" [105:1.8].

4. The Sevenfold I AM and the Seven Absolutes

The book describes the self-differentiation within the I AM in seven relationships [105:2.4]: the Universal Father (father of the Eternal Son), the Universal Controller (cause of Paradise), the Universal Creator (one with the Son, initiating creation), the Infinite Upholder (self-associative), the Infinite Potential (self-qualified), the Infinite Capacity (static-reactive), and the Universal One of Infinity [105:2.5-2.11]. These seven fundamental relationships are eternalized as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity [105:3.1]: the First, Second, and Third Sources and Centers, the Isle of Paradise, the Deity Absolute, the Unqualified Absolute, and the Universal Absolute [105:3.2-3.8].

5. Seven Realities without Beginning

What is important is that, although this is described like a story in time sequence, the Seven Absolutes are all unqualifiedly and co-ordinately eternal [105:3.1]. All absolute reality is from eternity and without beginning of existence; it is narrated sequentially only in order to present it to humans in time-space language [105:2.1]. The Seven Absolutes taken together equal infinity, yet the Universal Father himself is actually infinite [105:3.2].

6. What It Means for Our Faith

The book invites us, when we stand in awe before the vastness of the master universe, to consider that even this creation may be only a partial revelation of the Infinite [105:1.7]. Our concepts of infinity are growing even now and will continue to grow throughout our endless careers [105:1.8]. And the Father phase of the I AM can be partially experienced on spiritual levels, in worship, even by mortals still in the flesh [105:2.5].

Summary

The I AM is a philosophic postulate for thinking about the infinite origin of all reality, and in personal meanings it is synonymous with the Universal Father. The Father we know in worship is part of that infinity, but the face which the Infinite turns toward us is always the face of a loving Father [105:1.2, 105:1.6, 105:1.8].

q275.question: If the Thought Adjuster is not a personality, how can it have mind and will, and why does it submit to the human will?
q275.answer:
Paper 107 explains that although the Thought Adjuster is not a personality, it is a real entity, a "prepersonal" being possessed of powers commensurate with mind and the equivalent of will [107:7.1, 107:7.5]. And it says that the Adjuster submits to the human will because Adjuster volition, though absolute in nature, is prepersonal in manifestation, while the human will functions on the personality level [107:7.4].

1. Not a Personality, but a Real Entity

"⟦Q 107:7.1⟧Thought Adjusters are not personalities, but they are real entities⟦/Q⟧" [107:7.1]. They are perfectly individualized, yet while indwelling mortals they are never actually personalized; they are realities of the purest order known in the universe of universes, the divine presence [107:7.1]. It is not correct to call Adjusters subpersonal or superpersonal, but it is permissible to call them prepersonal beings [107:7.5].

2. Do Adjusters Have Minds?

It is hard for humans to understand that the Adjuster has a mind, because we know mind only as the mediator between spirit and matter. The Adjuster is a fragment of God on the absolute level of reality, prior to the segregation of energy and spirit, and needs no such mediating function [107:5.1]. Yet since Adjusters can plan, work, and love, they must have powers of selfhood commensurate with mind, and without mind they could never be personalized [107:5.2]. Their mindedness is said to be like that of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son [107:5.3]. Even after fusion, the mind of the Adjuster persists distinct from the mind of the creature until the ascender reaches spirit levels [107:5.5].

3. The Equivalent of Will

Adjusters volunteer to indwell, design the eternal careers of human beings, and adapt, modify, and substitute according to circumstances; all of this connotes genuine volition [107:7.3]. They have affection for mortals, function in universe crises, and are always ready to act decisively in accordance with human choice [107:7.3]. Yet the Solitary Messenger who presents this paper frankly admits that how an impersonal entity can choose and volunteer is a question easy to ask, but that probably no being has ever found the exact answer [107:7.2].

4. Why the Adjuster Submits to the Human Will

"⟦Q 107:7.4⟧Acreditamos que seja porque a volição do Ajustador, embora absoluta, por natureza, seja pré-pessoal na sua manifestação.⟦/Q⟧." [107:7.4] The human will functions on the personality level of universe reality, and throughout the cosmos the impersonal and the prepersonal are ever responsive to the will and acts of existent personality [107:7.4]. Therefore the Adjuster, though it comes from an infinite source, respects human free choice and works only through that choice.

5. More than Pure Spirit

Adjusters are spirits, pure spirits, presumably absolute spirits, but they are something more; in addition to conjectured mindedness, factors of pure energy are also present [107:6.4]. They traverse space over the gravity circuits of Paradise, yet they are not a result of gravity but fragments of the ancestor of gravity [107:6.4, 107:6.6]. Moreover, no Adjuster has ever been disloyal to the Paradise Father [107:4.3].

6. What It Means for Us

"⟦Q 107:6.2⟧O Ajustador é a possibilidade que o homem tem de eternidade; e o homem é a possibilidade que o Ajustador tem de ser uma personalidade.⟦/Q⟧." [107:6.2] The Adjusters truly and divinely love us and long to eternalize our temporal identity [107:6.2]. No limit can ever be placed on the destiny of this partnership of fusion with an actual fragment of the infinite Father [107:4.7].

Summary

The Adjuster is not a personality but a prepersonal reality; yet it possesses mind and the equivalent of will, comparable to the mindedness of the Father and the Son, and it plans and loves. But because its will is prepersonal in manifestation, it respects and follows the human will, which acts on the personality level. That is exactly why our choices determine our co-operation with the Adjuster and our eternal destiny [107:5.2, 107:7.3, 107:7.4].

q276.question: When, and under what conditions, does the Thought Adjuster come to a person, and what does it prepare before coming?
q276.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, the Thought Adjuster is actually assigned when the child makes the first moral personality decision, and on Urantia it arrives, on the average, just prior to the sixth birthday [108:2.1]. Long before that, however, the Adjuster has received full information about the person, has volunteered, and comes with a plan prepared to fit that mind [108:1.2, 108:1.8].

1. Volunteering and Selection

It is strongly believed that all Thought Adjusters are volunteers [108:1.2]. The seraphic drafts of ancestry and the projected patterns of life conduct are relayed by the technique of reflectivity to the Adjuster reserves on Divinington, including the hereditary background, the intellectual endowment, and an estimate of spiritual capacity [108:1.2]. The Adjuster is interested in three qualifications of the candidate: intellectual capacity, spiritual perception, and the degree to which the two combine to evolve a soul of survival value [108:1.3-1.6]. If more than one Adjuster volunteers, the supervising personalized order selects the one best suited, and the sex of the creature is not considered [108:1.7]. More experienced Adjusters often indwell higher types of minds, so human inheritance appears to be an important factor [108:1.1].

2. Preparation before Coming

Between volunteering and dispatch, the Adjuster is presumably instructed in the schools of Divinington, using a working pattern of the waiting mortal's mind, in the most effective plans for personality approach and mind spiritualization [108:1.8]. The Adjusters also come with a prearranged model career, an ideal life plan worked out with the Personalized Adjusters of Divinington; but no human being is under obligation to accept this plan [110:2.1]. After dispatch, the average transit time to Urantia is 117 hours, 42 minutes, and 7 seconds, virtually all of it occupied with registration on Uversa [108:1.9].

3. The First Moral Choice and the Seven Adjutant Spirits

The child's first moral choice is indicated in the seventh adjutant mind-spirit, registers instantly in the presence of the Master Spirit, and is forthwith dispatched to Divinington [108:2.1]. In the present generation that moment comes at "⟦Q 108:2.1⟧five years, ten months, and four days; that is, on the 2,134th day of terrestrial life⟦/Q⟧" [108:2.1]. For the Adjuster to enter, the co-ordinate function of all seven adjutants is required, and the mind must exhibit the worship outreach and the wisdom function of choosing between good and evil [108:2.2].

4. The Change since Pentecost

On planets where the Spirit of Truth functions, the Adjusters unfailingly come the moment the seventh adjutant begins to function, and so since the day of Pentecost Adjusters have been universally bestowed on all normal minds of moral status on Urantia [108:2.3]. And once they come, "⟦Q 108:2.4⟧Deus e o homem estão diretamente relacionados.⟦/Q⟧." [108:2.4] No intermediary stands between them [108:2.4].

5. Conditions before the Spirit of Truth

Before the Spirit of Truth was poured out, the following were observed to be associated with the arrival of Adjusters [108:2.5-2.11]: the assignment of a personal seraphic guardian, the attainment of the third psychic circle, a supreme decision of unusual spiritual import, the spirit of brotherhood devoted to unselfish ministry to one's fellows, and the decision to do quietly the will of the Father in heaven. In particular, Adjusters were observed to be dispatched immediately at the moment of that decision to do the Father's will [108:2.10].

6. What It Comes to Do

The Adjuster is a "heavenly helper" who works chiefly for the future life, not this life [108:5.5]. Rather than making life easy, it may make it reasonably difficult in order to stimulate decisions, yet it gives sublime peace of mind and tranquillity of spirit [108:5.5]. The Adjuster is an absolutely dependable guide who never falters [108:5.3].

Summary

The Adjuster knows everything about the person in advance, volunteers, prepares a fitting plan, and comes at the moment of the first moral decision. Since Pentecost every normal child on Urantia receives an Adjuster at an average age of about six, and from then on God and man are directly related without any intermediary [108:1.2, 108:2.1, 108:2.3, 108:2.4].

q277.question: What is a Personalized Adjuster, and what is the Adjuster that indwelt Jesus doing now?
q277.answer:
A Personalized Adjuster is a Thought Adjuster, originally a prepersonal entity without personality, who has received personality from the Universal Father through the experience of serving personal beings [109:7.1]. The Adjuster that indwelt Jesus is such a being and now directs all Adjuster activities in the local universe of Nebadon [109:6.4].

1. How They Are Personalized

Fragments of the Father of the Adjuster type attain personality only by acquiring personal attributes through service-ministry to personal beings [109:7.1]. Paper 107 describes Personalized Adjusters as those who have served with incarnated Paradise Sons, together with Monitors who achieved unusual distinction during indwelling but whose subjects rejected survival [107:2.8]. Adjusters who volunteer for bestowal missions know that they cannot attain personality by that service alone, yet the Father of spirits often bestows personality upon them and appoints them as directors [109:6.3].

2. A Failed Career Is Not in Vain

When a human rejects survival, the Adjuster departs carrying away everything of survival value that has evolved in that mind [109:6.2]. If such an Adjuster, after repeated failures to attain fusion through the nonsurvival of successive subjects, is personalized, it becomes "⟦Q 109:6.2⟧a composite assembly of all the survival traits of all his former creature hosts⟦/Q⟧" [109:6.2]. The book therefore says that no worth-while experience is lost and no true meaning or real value ever perishes [109:6.1].

3. Their Nature and Role

Personalized Adjusters make Divinington their home and instruct and direct their prepersonal fellows [109:7.1]. They are the untrammeled, sovereign stabilizers and compensators of the universes, combining the existential and the experiential, time and eternity [109:7.2]. They are also the executives of the Architects of the Master Universe and the personal agents for all the ministry of the Universal Father [109:7.3]. As "omnipersonal" beings, before personality, personality, and after personality, they are the only beings who embrace all the known relationships of personality [109:7.4]. On Divinington they receive names rather than numbers [107:3.10].

4. Jesus' Adjuster

The Adjuster activities of Nebadon are directed by Michael's Personalized Adjuster, the very Monitor who guided him step by step when he lived as Joshua ben Joseph [109:6.4]. This Adjuster had earlier served with Machiventa Melchizedek in the days of Abraham [109:6.4]. He triumphed in Jesus' human mind, a mind that in every situation was consecrated to the Father's will, saying, "⟦Q 109:6.5⟧Not my will, but yours, be done⟦/Q⟧" [109:6.5]. Today this Adjuster reflects the humanity of Jesus before his baptism, a living transcript of the eternal values achieved in an ordinary life [109:6.6]. The Adjuster training schools of Divinington are likewise presided over by the Personalized Adjuster of the first Paradise Son of the Michael order to complete his sevenfold bestowal [107:3.9].

5. Activities on Urantia

When the Most High custodian of Urantia assumed an emergency regency, three Personalized Adjusters whom he had neither chosen nor expected appeared at once, and they were said to be the most active of all the celestial beings then ministering on Urantia [109:7.7]. Much of their ministry, however, may not be discussed with Adjuster-indwelt mortals, and no one can forecast their future missions [109:7.8].

Summary

A Personalized Adjuster is an Adjuster who has received personality from the Father through the experience of serving humans and divine Sons; carrying all the survival values of the lives it has indwelt, it works as a personal agent of the Universal Father. The Adjuster who guided Jesus, bearing that experience, now directs all Adjuster activities in Nebadon [109:6.2, 109:6.4, 109:7.3].

q278.question: May I regard the voice of conscience, dreams, or thoughts that come to me suddenly as the voice of the Thought Adjuster?
q278.answer:
The Urantia Book clearly warns against readily identifying any of these three as the voice of the Adjuster. Conscience is a human reaction not directly related to the Adjuster, ordinary dreams are purely physiologic and psychologic phenomena, and most sudden thoughts also arise from the subconscious [110:5.1, 110:5.5, 110:4.3]. The influence of the Adjuster is for the most part, though not wholly, a superconscious experience [110:5.5].

1. Conscience and the Adjuster

"⟦Q 110:5.1⟧A consciência é um fenômeno humano e uma reação puramente psíquica.⟦/Q⟧." [110:5.1] Conscience is not to be despised, but it is hardly the voice of God to the soul [110:5.1]. The book explains the difference this way: conscience admonishes you to do right, but the Adjuster, in addition, endeavors to tell you what truly is right [110:5.1]. Paper 100 likewise defines conscience as criticism of oneself by one's own value-habits and personal ideals [100:1.5].

2. Are Dreams Messages from the Adjuster?

The disorderly dreams of the unco-ordinated sleeping mind actually show the failure of the Adjusters to harmonize the elements of the human mind [110:5.2]. The Adjuster does work during sleep, but it attempts to accomplish only what has already been sanctioned by the decisions and choices made while awake [110:5.3]. In dreams our own passions and urges enter into the picture and turn the divine message into an expression of unexpressed desires [110:5.4]. Thus, "⟦Q 110:5.5⟧É extremamente perigoso postular qualquer coisa, quanto à participação do Ajustador, no conteúdo da vida nos sonhos.⟦/Q⟧." [110:5.5]

3. Sudden Thoughts and Inspiration

Some sudden thoughts or conclusions may at times be the activity of the Adjuster, but far more often they are the normal mental function of submerged ideas rising into consciousness [110:4.3]. The revelations of the Adjuster come through the superconscious, not the subconscious [110:4.3]. We are not able to distinguish the products of our own material intellect from those of the joint activities of the soul and the Adjuster [110:4.2], and much of what is received as the voice of the Adjuster is more often really the emanation of one's own intellect [110:5.6].

4. The Danger of Mistaking Them

Even when the Adjuster flashes a gleam of new truth, it has sometimes so blinded the creature as to precipitate a convulsion of fanaticism, and many new religions and strange "isms" have arisen from the aborted and distorted communications of Adjusters [110:4.5]. So the book gives a surprising counsel: it is better to err by rejecting an Adjuster's expression as a purely human experience than to blunder into exalting a reaction of the mortal mind to the sphere of divine dignity [110:5.5]. This danger zone must be discerned by each person through human wisdom and superhuman insight [110:5.6].

5. How, Then, Do We Work with the Adjuster?

Co-operation with the Adjuster is not a particularly conscious process; our motives, decisions, faithful determinations, and supreme desires constitute real co-operation [110:3.6]. We can augment harmony by choosing to respond to divine leading, by loving God and desiring to be like him, by loving and serving man, and by joyfully accepting cosmic citizenship [110:3.7-3.10]. Problems of the mind beyond the level of consciousness may be left to the keeping of the Adjusters, who will in time resurrect the values entrusted to them [110:4.4]. It is recorded that even the human being who served as the channel of this revelation benefited from his almost complete indifference to Adjuster phenomena [110:5.7].

Summary

Conscience is a human reaction, dreams are usually physiologic and psychologic phenomena, and thoughts that come to mind are mostly the products of our own minds. Since the Adjuster's work is done quietly, mainly in the superconscious, the safe and true way is not to exalt a particular voice or dream into divine revelation but to co-operate through the decision to do the Father's will and through loving service [110:3.6, 110:5.1, 110:5.5].

q279.question: What is the "soul" in The Urantia Book, and how is it related to the mind and the Thought Adjuster?
q279.answer:
In The Urantia Book the soul is not an entity that comes into a person already complete at birth; it is a new reality that the human material mind and the indwelling Thought Adjuster grow together through the person's choices. Its nature is neither material nor spiritual but "morontial," and it is the embryo of the future vehicle that will carry on the identity of the personality after death [111:2.7, 111:3.2].

1. The Three Factors That Make Up the Soul

Not two but three factors are at work in the evolution of the soul [111:2.4]. The first is the human mind and all the cosmic influences acting on it [111:2.5]; the second is the divine spirit indwelling that mind, with its potentials [111:2.6]; and the third is the relationship between the material mind and the divine spirit. "⟦Q 111:2.7⟧A realidade dessa relação única não é nem material nem espiritual, mas moroncial. É a alma.⟦/Q⟧." [111:2.7] The soul is not a mere combination of the two elements but an entirely new and unique universe value with the potential of eternal persistence [111:2.3].

2. The Mind Is the Loom, the Adjuster the Weaver

The book offers a beautiful image. The material mind of mortal man is the cosmic loom that carries the morontia fabrics, and on them the Thought Adjuster threads the spirit patterns of a character of enduring values and divine meanings [111:2.2]. The mind is the arena in which the human personality chooses or rejects God, making itself eternal or destroying itself [111:1.3]. The soul is therefore called the "joint offspring" of an adjutant mind, dominated by a human will that craves to know God, and the Adjuster [111:2.10]. The midway creatures have called this soul the "mid-mind," between the material mind and the cosmic mind [111:2.8].

3. Growth Determined by the Will

The soul, the morontia self, faithfully portrays the harvest of the temporal decisions the mortal self is making [111:1.5]. It is not what the mind comprehends but what it desires to comprehend that insures survival, and it is not so much being God-conscious as longingly seeking God that results in universe ascension [111:1.5]. The book also says, "⟦Q 111:1.9⟧A mente é a vossa embarcação, o Ajustador é o vosso piloto, a vontade humana é o capitão.⟦/Q⟧." [111:1.9] The Adjuster guides a person's mind but does not dominate it against his will [111:1.8].

4. The Soul's Evolution and Our Mistakes

The mistakes and wrong conduct of the mortal mind may delay the evolution of the soul, but they cannot inhibit that phenomenon once it has been initiated by the Adjuster with the consent of the will [111:3.1]. A person can, however, refuse survival both before death and after survival, up until fusion with the Adjuster [111:3.1]. In proportion to its growth the soul becomes increasingly conscious of both mind and Adjuster, and it persistently evolves toward increasing spirit control [111:3.4]. The mortal career is not so much a probation as an education [111:3.5].

5. The Soul after Death

During life the power of decision resides in the material mind, but as one grows, the self becomes more and more identified with the emerging morontia soul, and after the resurrection on the mansion worlds it is wholly identified with the morontia self [111:3.2]. The soul is at first morontial, but it eventually ascends to the level of true spirit and usually fuses with the spirit of the Universal Father that initiated its creation [111:3.3]. The more the soul is permeated by truth, beauty, and goodness, the more indestructible its existence becomes [111:3.7].

Summary

The soul is a morontia reality born of the relationship between the material mind and the Thought Adjuster; it grows through our choices to seek God and becomes the new vehicle of the personality after death. The mind is the loom, the Adjuster is the weaver, and the will is the captain who permits the work. Therefore, "⟦Q 111:3.7⟧What you begin in time you will assuredly finish in eternity—if it is worth finishing⟦/Q⟧." [111:3.7]

q280.question: What are the three kinds of death described in The Urantia Book, and can we communicate with the dead or keep our earthly memories?
q280.answer:
From the standpoint of personality survival, The Urantia Book distinguishes three kinds of death: spiritual (soul) death, intellectual (mind) death, and physical (body and mind) death [112:3.1-3.4]. It says that the dead are wholly unconscious until the resurrection and so do not communicate with people on earth, and that on awakening in the mansion worlds they retain the memories that have spiritual meaning and the memories of personality relationships [112:3.7, 112:5.22].

1. Spiritual (Soul) Death

When a mortal has finally rejected survival and has been pronounced spiritually insolvent and morontially bankrupt in the conjoint opinion of the Adjuster and the seraphim, and this has been verified, the indwelling Adjuster is immediately released [112:3.2]. This kind of death is final in its significance, even if the body and mind temporarily go on living. "⟦Q 112:3.2⟧From the cosmic standpoint the mortal is already dead⟦/Q⟧" [112:3.2].

2. Intellectual (Mind) Death

When the vital circuits of higher adjutant ministry are disrupted through the aberrations of intellect or the destruction of the brain mechanism, and this condition passes the irreparable point, the Adjuster is immediately released and departs for Divinington [112:3.3]. A body without volitional mind is no longer human, but according to the choices previously made, the soul may survive [112:3.3]. This is a comforting passage when we think of the destiny of those who suffer from diseases or injuries of the mind.

3. Physical (Body and Mind) Death

In death as we commonly know it, the Adjuster remains in the citadel of the mind until it ceases to function as an intelligent mechanism, about the time when the measurable brain energies cease their rhythmic vital pulsations [112:3.4]. The Adjuster then goes to Divinington bearing the memory transcription of the mortal career, and the immortal morontia soul remains in the keeping of the guardian of destiny [112:3.5]. Upon death the Adjuster temporarily loses personality but not identity, and the human subject temporarily loses identity but not personality; the two reunite on the mansion worlds [112:3.7].

4. Can We Communicate with the Dead?

The book's answer is clear. Souls without Adjusters are wholly unconscious during the long or short sleep of death, and no exhibition of personality or ability to communicate can occur until survival is completed [112:3.7]. "⟦Q 112:3.7⟧Àqueles que vão para os mundos das mansões não lhes é permitido enviar mensagens de volta aos seus seres queridos.⟦/Q⟧" [112:3.7], and it is the policy throughout the universes to forbid such communication during the current dispensation [112:3.7]. Moreover, a departed Adjuster never returns to earth as the being of former indwelling [112:3.7]. From death until repersonalization the soul rests unconscious in the keeping of the seraphic guardian of destiny [112:5.13].

5. Memory after Awakening

On awakening in the mansion worlds, the great change makes much of the former life seem at first like a vague dream, but in time many associations become clear [112:5.21]. The Adjuster rehearses only those memories and experiences essential to the universe career, and memories having neither spiritual meaning nor morontia value perish with the material brain [112:5.22]. But "⟦Q 112:5.22⟧personality and the relationships between personalities are never scaffolding⟦/Q⟧" [112:5.22]. Memory of personality relationships has cosmic value and will persist, and on the mansion worlds we will recognize and remember our former associates and be remembered by them [112:5.22].

6. A Fair and Merciful Judgment

Even if environmental handicaps kept someone from mastering levels of growth on earth, if there are intentions and desires of survival value, extended probation is granted [112:5.6], and in cases of doubt the universe government always rules in the interest of the individual [112:5.7]. Every will creature will experience one real opportunity to make a final choice [112:5.9].

Summary

There is spiritual death through the rejection of survival, intellectual death through the destruction of the mind circuits, and physical death of body and mind. The dead remain unconscious until the resurrection and do not communicate with earth, but after awakening they retain the spiritually valuable memories and their relationships with those they loved [112:3.1, 112:3.7, 112:5.22].

q281.question: To whom, and by what standard, are guardian angels assigned, and what do they actually do in our lives?
q281.answer:
The Urantia Book says that the teaching about guardian angels is not a myth but a fact [113:1.1]. Not everyone has a personal angel from the beginning, however; since Michael's bestowal, seraphim are assigned according to human intelligence, spirituality, and destiny [113:1.2]. Guardian angels do not manipulate our will; they guard and teach us mainly through our outward environment [113:4.1, 113:5.1].

1. The Standard of Assignment: The Psychic Circles

For average persons, seraphim are assigned according to their attainment of the circles of human intellectuality and spirituality [113:1.6]. In the seventh circle one guardian angel with a company of cherubim cares for a thousand mortals; in the sixth circle a seraphic pair cares for five hundred; in the fifth circle, about one hundred; and in the fourth circle, ten [113:1.7]. When the third circle is reached, a personal angel (in reality two) is wholly devoted to that person [113:1.8]. Even those of subnormal mind have a company of seraphim and a battalion of cherubim assigned to see that justice and mercy are extended to them [113:1.3].

2. Guardians of Destiny

Seraphim are not called guardians of destiny until a person has made a supreme decision to become Godlike, has entered the third circle, or has been mustered into the reserve corps of destiny [113:2.1]. The first mortal on Urantia to secure a personal guardian was Rantowoc, a wise man of the red race [113:2.2]. All assignments are made from among volunteering seraphim, and only seraphim of long service and proven ability become guardians of destiny [113:2.3]. The book gives the example of more than one hundred seraphim volunteering for one person, of whom one pair was chosen [113:2.7]. One of the pair becomes the recording angel [113:2.9].

3. What They Do

Seraphim do not work from within through the soul, as the Adjusters do; they work from without inward, through the social, ethical, and moral environment, seeking to foster the decisions that make up the circles of progress [113:4.1]. If the Adjuster is the essence of man's eternal nature, the seraphim are the teachers of his evolving nature [113:4.2]. The urge to pray that God-conscious persons often feel is frequently the result of seraphic influence [113:4.4]. The guardians also personally co-ordinate the many impersonal spirit influences that touch mind and soul, and they have the gift of combining the love of the Father with the mercy of the Son [113:3.1, 113:3.3]. They do not seem to communicate directly with the Adjusters, yet the two work in perfect harmony, and the guardians are most active when the Adjusters are least active [113:4.5].

4. What They Do Not Do

"⟦Q 113:5.1⟧Angels do not invade the sanctity of the human mind; they do not manipulate the will of mortals⟦/Q⟧" [113:5.1], and no angel has authority to curtail the prerogatives of human choosing [113:5.1]. They are not directly concerned with our requests or prayers but act on the mandates of their superiors [113:5.3]. They are guardians only, not dictators or directors; once we have set our own course, they help us make the best use of it, and ordinarily they intervene only in emergencies [113:5.4]. So to accept seraphic guidance is more likely to mean meeting the rugged hills of moral choosing and spiritual progress than living an easy life [113:4.3].

5. The Hearts of the Angels

The angels develop an abiding affection for their human associates and share most of our emotions [113:2.5]. The one emotion they find hard to understand is the legacy of animal fear; they find it difficult to see why we allow even our religious faith to be dominated by fear [113:2.5]. Between death and resurrection, the seraphic guardian becomes the personal custodian of the mind patterns, memory formulas, and soul realities [113:3.4].

Summary

Guardian angels are not a myth but real ministers assigned according to progress in the psychic circles and according to spiritual decisions. A personal guardian of destiny is given at the third circle, at a supreme decision, or upon entry into the reserve corps of destiny, and they teach and guard us through our environment without invading our will. Their ministry bears its best fruit when we live by faith instead of fear [113:1.8, 113:2.1, 113:5.1].

q282.question: What does it mean that God the Supreme grows in dependence on our human choices and experiences, and what significance does this have for our lives?
q282.answer:
Paper 117 introduces God the Supreme as "God in time," a finite Deity who is still evolving toward completion [117:2.1, 117:4.1]. Because part of that evolution is predicated on the wisdom and choices of every personality [117:4.2], it says: "⟦Q 117:4.9⟧That Supreme Deity is in a certain sense dependent on the choosing of the mortal will⟦/Q⟧." [117:4.9] This means that our ordinary decisions of faith have cosmic significance.

1. A God Who Grows

The Supreme is the one in whom is secreted the growth of creatures in time, the culminating result of all finite growth [117:2.1]. We ourselves are able to grow because we are in the Supreme and are participating in his cycle of growth [117:2.5]. So the book regards the incompleteness of the Supreme as a virtue that makes the growth of creatures possible: "⟦Q 117:2.8⟧O vazio tem a sua virtude, pois pode ser experiencialmente preenchido.⟦/Q⟧." [117:2.8]

2. Our Choices Make Up the Supreme

When a human being chooses eternal survival, he is cocreating destiny, and in his life the finite God finds an increased measure of self-realization and sovereignty [117:4.2]. The progress of the Adjuster in spiritualizing a human personality is directly productive of an enlargement of the sovereignty of the Supreme [117:4.9]. Conversely, if a creature rejects the eternal career, that part of the Supreme which was dependent on his choice experiences delay, and the personality of the nonsurvivor returns to the Supreme as a drop of water returns to the sea [117:4.2, 117:4.4]. The book sums it up: "⟦Q 117:4.12⟧Pois, se o homem alcança o destino humano, assim também o Supremo alcançará o destino nos níveis da deidade.⟦/Q⟧." [117:4.12]

3. The Irreplaceable Worth of the Individual

An individual personality is insignificant in comparison with the whole of Supremacy, yet each human personality has an irreplaceable meaning and value in the finite [117:4.5]. If we reject survival, another creature will someday contribute in his own way, "⟦Q 117:4.10⟧Esta, porém, seria a contribuição dela para o Supremo, não a vossa.⟦/Q⟧." [117:4.10] This reciprocal relationship is the basis of cosmic morality, the morality that recognizes duty to experiential Deity [117:4.8].

4. Participation without Loss of Personality

Becoming one with the Supreme does not mean that we lose our individuality. The personalities who participate in the actualization of the finite God do not lose their volitional selfhood but are progressively augmented [117:5.2]. Yet because the repercussions of all experience form part of the divine experiencing of the Supreme, the book quotes the saying, "⟦Q 117:5.5⟧“O ato é nosso, as conseqüências são de Deus.”⟦/Q⟧." [117:5.5] When we act, the Supreme reacts, and this constitutes the fact of progress [117:5.6].

5. God as Father and as Mother

Just as God is our divine Father, the Supreme is our divine Mother, in whom we are nurtured throughout our universe careers [117:6.2]. The evolving soul is the child of the Father's Adjuster action and the cosmic reaction of the Supreme Being [117:6.5]. But while the Father can be discovered in one's own heart, the Supreme must be searched for in the hearts of all other men [117:6.23], for brotherly affection is the essence of the love of the Supreme [117:6.10].

6. What It Means for the Life of Faith

As we strive for self-expression, the Supreme is striving in us for Deity expression, and as we seek the Father, the Supreme also seeks the Paradise Creator [117:4.6]. When a man consecrates his will to the doing of the Father's will, God makes that man more than he is [117:4.14]. And no God-knowing mortal can ever be lonely, for the very way that he is traversing is the presence of the Supreme [117:6.27].

Summary

God the Supreme is a finite Deity who is being completed through the experiences and choices of all creatures. Our decision to do God's will therefore goes beyond personal salvation to a participation in completing the God of the universe, and that participation is carried out in brotherly love and service [117:4.2, 117:4.9, 117:6.10].

q283.question: What does The Urantia Book mean by "providence," and has God determined in advance everything that happens in my life?
q283.answer:
The Urantia Book states plainly that providence does not mean that God has decided everything for us in advance. "⟦Q 118:10.1⟧Deus nos ama demais para fazer isso, pois isso não seria nada menos do que tirania cósmica.⟦/Q⟧." [118:10.1] Man does have relative powers of choice [118:10.1]. Providence is not a power that magically manipulates the affairs of individuals; it is God's overcontrol that leads the whole universe toward its goals, and it is still in the process of being completed [118:10.4, 118:10.23].

1. Providence Is a Function Related to the Total

The Gods have attributes but the Trinity has functions, and providence too is a function: the composite of the other-than-personal overcontrol of the universe of universes [118:10.4]. Because providence functions with regard to the total, providential intervention indicates that a being's function is important to the evolutionary growth of some total, such as a race, a nation, or a planet [118:10.5]. "⟦Q 118:10.5⟧É a importância da criatura na sua função que ocasiona a intervenção providencial, não a importância da criatura como pessoa.⟦/Q⟧." [118:10.5]

2. Is the Individual Then Forsaken?

No. God loves each creature as a child, and that love overshadows each creature throughout all time and eternity [118:10.5]. The Father, as a person, motivated by love, can at any time put forth a fatherly hand in the stream of cosmic events [118:10.6]. The Father's love is also a personal relationship acting directly in the heart of each individual, independent of the actions of other individuals [118:10.11]. That is, personal love comes through the Father and the Adjusters, while providence for the whole comes through the Supreme and the Trinity [118:10.11].

3. The Limits of What We Call Providence

The book points out that what men call providence is all too often the product of their own imagination, the fortuitous juxtaposition of chance circumstances [118:10.7]. Much of what is called good luck might really be bad luck; unearned leisure and undeserved wealth may be the greatest of afflictions; and an apparently cruel fate may in reality be the tempering fire that transmutes immature personality into the steel of real character [118:10.9]. Providence must therefore be partial and unpredictable at the present stage, because the actualization of the Supreme Being is incomplete and creature attitudes are ever changing [118:10.20-10.22].

4. Prayer and Providence

"⟦Q 118:10.23⟧Quando os homens oram pela intervenção da providência nas circunstâncias da vida, muitas vezes, a resposta às suas orações é uma mudança nas suas próprias atitudes perante a vida.⟦/Q⟧." [118:10.23] Providence is not whimsical or magical; it is the slow and sure emergence of the Supreme, the mighty sovereign of the finite universes [118:10.23]. Even now we can foretaste providence by pondering the fact that all things, be they good or evil, work together for the advancement of God-knowing mortals in their quest for the Father [118:10.18].
