5. Foreknowledge Does Not Abolish Freedom

On the question of predestination and foreknowledge the book keeps to the same principle. Just as a mature person's accurate forecast of a young associate's decision takes nothing from the freedom of that decision, so ultimate foreknowledge does not abrogate finite volition [118:7.1]. The Gods have wisely limited the range of immature will, but within those limits the will is genuine will, and choice becomes more and more free as one ascends [118:7.1, 118:7.8].

6. How Providence Becomes Clear

Providence becomes increasingly discernible as men reach upward from the material to the spiritual, and as spiritual insight deepens, one detects harmony in what was formerly chaos [118:10.19]. On a planet settled in light and life, providence becomes a reality because men live in accordance with the currents of the universe [118:10.16]. When the kingdom of God becomes real in the hearts of all men, that is the attained sovereignty of the Supreme Being [118:10.17].

Summary

Providence is not a fatalism that fixes everything in advance; it is God's overcontrol, still emerging, which leads the whole universe toward its goal while respecting our freedom. For the individual, the personal love of the Father works directly, and the more we grow spiritually, the more clearly we recognize providence in the events of our lives [118:10.1, 118:10.11, 118:10.19].

q284.question: What six bestowals did Michael pass through before coming to Urantia, and what did each of the seven bestowals reveal?
q284.answer:
Paper 119 relates that Michael, the Creator Son of Nebadon, had already bestowed himself upon his own universe six times, in the likeness of six different orders of creatures, before he lived as Jesus on Urantia. The seven bestowals took place at intervals of about one hundred and fifty million years, and the last of them was on Urantia [119:0.7]. Their purpose was that the Creator Son should gain the creature viewpoint by actual experience and so become a wise, sympathetic, and understanding sovereign [119:0.4, 119:0.6].

1. Why the Bestowals Were Necessary

A Creator Son pledges to the Trinity that he will not assume full sovereignty until his seven creature bestowals have been certified by the Ancients of Days [119:0.3]. He is by nature just, but through the bestowal experience he acquires understanding mercy [119:0.4]; the bestowals are not essential to the efficient administration of a universe, but they are absolutely necessary to the fair and merciful administration of a creation filled with imperfect creatures [119:0.5]. "⟦Q 119:8.2⟧Michael nasceu um criador, foi educado como um administrador e aperfeiçoado como um executivo; no entanto, foi-lhe pedido que conquistasse a sua própria soberania, por meio da experiência.⟦/Q⟧." [119:8.2]

2. The First through Third Bestowals

The first was the Melchizedek bestowal. About one billion years ago a strange Melchizedek Son appeared, carried out twenty-four emergency assignments, and by common consent became the chief of the Melchizedeks [119:1.1, 119:1.3-1.5]. The second was the Lanonandek bestowal: in place of Lutentia, the System Sovereign who had rebelled, he became the acting System Sovereign, ruled the confused system in justice and mercy, and became known as "⟦Q 119:2.5⟧the Savior Sovereign of the system of Palonia⟦/Q⟧" [119:2.4, 119:2.5]. The third was the Material Son bestowal, in which he became the acting Planetary Prince on planet 217 in another system that had rebelled [119:3.1, 119:3.3].

3. The Fourth through Sixth Bestowals

The fourth was the seraphic bestowal: for a period of over forty years, as a seraphic teaching counselor, he was attached to twenty-six master teachers and functioned on twenty-two worlds [119:4.2, 119:4.3]. The fifth was the bestowal in which he appeared on Uversa as an unnumbered ascendant pilgrim named Eventod, that is, as a spirit mortal, tried and tested like his fellows [119:5.1, 119:5.2]. The sixth was the bestowal in which he lived as a morontia mortal on the headquarters of constellation five; it was one of the most extraordinary epochs of all, but the narrator says he is forbidden to reveal its details [119:6.3].

4. The Seventh, the Urantia Bestowal

The announcement that Urantia had been chosen as the world of the seventh bestowal came shortly after the default of Adam and Eve became known [119:7.2]. Because he had always before appeared as a fully developed individual, the broadcast that he had been born in Bethlehem as a helpless infant sent a thrill through Salvington [119:7.3]. After this bestowal Michael was proclaimed the settled ruler of Nebadon [119:8.1].

5. What Each Bestowal Revealed

Each bestowal revealed one aspect of the will of Deity as personalized in the Seven Master Spirits [119:8.4].

Melchizedek bestowal: the united will of the Father, Son, and Spirit
Lanonandek bestowal: the will of the Father and the Son
Adamic bestowal: the will of the Father and the Spirit
Seraphic bestowal: the will of the Son and the Spirit
Uversa mortal bestowal: the will of the Conjoint Actor
Morontia mortal bestowal: the will of the Eternal Son
Urantia bestowal: the will of the Universal Father, as a mortal of flesh and blood

The sum of the seven bestowals is a new Nebadon revelation of the Supreme Being, and by them Michael also augmented the evolving sovereignty of God the Supreme [119:8.3, 119:8.5].

6. What It Means for Us

Because Urantia is the place where all these bestowals were completed, it has become known throughout all Nebadon [119:8.2], and it is called the sentimental shrine of all Nebadon [119:8.8]. Our sovereign is one who has personally experienced creature life on every level: a Melchizedek minister, a system savior, an Adamic redeemer, a seraphic fellow, an associate of ascending spirits, a morontia progressor, and a Son of Man in the likeness of mortal flesh [119:8.8].

Summary

Michael bestowed himself six times, as a Melchizedek, a Lanonandek, a Material Son, a seraphim, a spirit mortal, and a morontia mortal, and then was born as a babe on Urantia to complete the seventh bestowal. Each bestowal was a living out of one aspect of the divine will, and through that experience he became a merciful sovereign who truly understands his creatures [119:0.4, 119:8.2, 119:8.4].
